The lowest common ancestors of Methotrexate and Lamivudine are identified as Enzyme Inhibitor and Organic Heterocyclic Compound, suggesting a shared functional category. These pathways imply that Methotrexate may influence the activity of Abcc4 through its interaction with Lamivudine, potentially altering the transport function of Abcc4. The evidence highlights a possible mechanism where Methotrexate indirectly affects Abcc4 via Lamivudine, though the exact nature of this interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
